text:
Maya: ran an nsys trace on the repro for the kv-cache write hotspot we saw yesterday. comparing flash-v2 vs fused-attn variant. main surprising thing: write_kv_store kernel is taking ~30-45% of GPU time and shows bursts that align with a cudaMemcpy from CPU -> GPU :eyes:
perf-bot: nsys report uploaded: https://perf.example/redwood/1839123456 (nsys + perfetto link) :link:
Rishi: can you paste the nsys CLI you used? also which model/config (seq, batch)
Maya: sure. repro config: seq_len=2048, batch=6 (mixed lengths: 512/1024/2048), model=redwood/open-2-like, kv_sharding=off
Maya: nsys run I used:
```
nsys profile --trace=cuda,cudnn,nvtx --output=trace_1839123456 \
  --sample=none --cpuctxsw=0 --capture-range=cudaProfilerApi \
  python -m runtime.benchmark --model open-redwood --seq 2048 --batch 6
```
Ben: timeline shows repeated short bursts where write_kv_store launches and then a long gap where nothing else is using SMs. looks like write serialization + small-ish memcpy synchronous stall
Alex: that pattern smells like we fall back to CPU-side packing for some batches. did kernel selection pick flash-v2 for those calls or the fused fallback?
Maya: flash-v2 chosen for most forward-attn calls but for kv write we see `flash_to_shadow_store` kernel variant being used a lot. a few runs show fused-attn path avoids the heavy write kernel but has higher latency elsewhere
Diego: here's the kernel selection snippet I instrumented in runtime (pseudo):
```
if (seq_len > 1024 && batch <= 8) use_flash_v2();
else if (kv_cache_enabled && mixed_lengths) use_shadow_store();
```
Diego: that `mixed_lengths` branch was added as a cheap guard for memory blowups, might be the culprit
Carla: mixed_lengths grouping is blunt. we should bucket by seq_len and route per-bucket to kernel variants instead of a global mixed_lengths flag. that avoids forcing shadow_store for the whole micro-batch
Rishi: agree. also we saw large PCIe activity in perfetto. can we confirm whether those memcpy peaks are `cudaMemcpy` (sync) or `cudaMemcpyAsync` + stream syncs?
Maya: perfetto shows host->device peaks coincident with write_kv_store start. nvtx ranges from our runtime mark the write start, then a `cudaMemcpy` shortly after. looks synchronous.
Ben: synchronous memcpy is the killer. either we're copying KV shards back to host or touching pinned pages in a blocking way. check for `thrust::copy` or accidental readback in the write path
Alex: there was a defensive path that materializes small tensors on host to compute offsets for weird shapes. if mixed_lengths true we do shape normalization on CPU. that would explain it
Carla: quick mitigation: 1) change batching heuristic to group equal seq lengths aggressively, 2) change shape-normalization to run on GPU where possible, 3) add KV write async + cudaEvent to avoid stream stalls
Maya: I'll prototype: - bucket requests by seq_len before kernel pick - change shape_norm to CUDA kernel or device memcpy - instrument nvtx around all memcpy ops
Rishi: for instrumentation, add `cudaMemcpyAsync(..., stream)` + `cudaEventRecord` and capture with nsys. also add `NVTX_RANGE` around the high-level `write_kv_store` so perfetto shows user ranges
Maya: good plan. i'll push a small trace branch and run a 3x sweep (seq 512/1024/2048) with batch 6 and mixed distribution, then post the perfetto links
perf-bot: quick summary from first nsys: flash-v2 forward kernels: 42% GPU time, write_kv_store: 33% GPU time, memcpy H2D: 18% (synchronous), kernel occupancy avg 62%
Ben: if memcpy H2D is 18% that's huge. likely we're writing back intermediate KV shapes to host then reupload. maybe metadata serialization to protobuf is running in the hot path?
Diego: I remember a recent change that serialized per-request metadata for debugging when `KV_CHECKSUM` env var was set. could that be on in this CI repro?
Maya: nope env was clean. but runtime debug path still has a fallthrough that packs headers in host memory for mixed lengths. i'll remove that fallback for the next run
Carla: aside from code changes, we should consider improving kernel selection heuristic: prefer fused-attn for batches with >30% short sequences because flash-v2's write pattern penalizes mixed shapes. also allow dynamic per-batch override after first step profiling
Rishi: dynamic per-batch override is good: run the first micro-batch with a lightweight profiler (a couple of iterations) then pick kernel variant for remaining micro-batches based on observed write/mem ratio
Maya: noted. going to: 1) remove host-side packing fallback; 2) add seq_len bucketing; 3) add async memcpy + NVTX; 4) run nsys sweeps and share links. target to have traces by EOD PST
Alex: thanks. if you can also dump kernel names + durations as a CSV from nsys (use `nsys-cupti` or `nsys stats --format csv`) that'll help quantify regression deltas
Maya: will do. thanks all. :thumbsup:
